title: The "Anything Else" Rule
summary: One rule can decide every transaction that has no rule of its own.
lesson: Anything else decides only what no other rule covers, and a specific rule always wins.
oneLiner: One rule can decide every transaction that has no rule of its own.
explain: The Anything else rule, also called the catch-all, sits at the bottom of the rulebook. It decides only when no other rule matches.
A common choice is a co-signer: anything new needs a second opinion before it runs.
A specific rule always wins over Anything else. Always Deny on one action blocks it, whatever the catch-all says.
takeaway: Anything else decides only what no other rule covers, and a specific rule always wins.

steps.label: Send Erin 1 ETH
steps.note: No rule mentions ETH, so Anything else decides. It wants the co-signer, who has not agreed.

steps.label: Send Erin 1 ETH, co-signed
steps.note: The co-signer agreed, so Anything else allows it.

steps.label: Approve Mallory to spend 1000 USDC, co-signed
steps.note: Letting someone spend USDC has its own rule, Always Deny. It wins, so the co-signer cannot help.
